title: Cultural Adaptation within Repeated Social Interactions
abstract: arXiv:2611.08334v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Much of human culture is tacit and is typically learned through situated social interaction. As LLMs are deployed as interactive agents across diverse communities, assessing their cultural competence demands moving beyond existing question-answering approaches, shifting from what they know to how they adapt. In this work, we broaden the scope of cultural adaptation in NLP by investigating whether LLMs can adapt through repeated interactions via a sandbox environment. By reframing cultural adaptation as a continuous process of norm assimilation through social interaction, our work demonstrates that memory mechanisms foster longitudinal learning across repeated interactions, facilitate transfer to different social settings, and enable multilingual norm assimilation across five languages. Together, our findings lay the groundwork for continuous, interaction-driven cultural adaptation in LLMs.

translated_title: 重复社会互动中的文化适应
translated_abstract: 人类文化大部分是隐性的（默会的），通常需要通过情境化的社会互动来习得。随着大语言模型（LLM）被部署为跨不同社区的交互式智能体，评估其文化胜任力需要超越现有的问答式方法，即从评估它们“知道什么”转向它们“如何适应”。在本工作中，我们通过沙盒环境研究LLM能否通过重复互动进行适应，从而拓宽了NLP领域中文化适应的研究范围。通过将文化适应重新定义为通过社会互动持续吸收规范的动态过程，我们的工作表明，记忆机制能够促进跨重复互动的纵向学习，支持向不同社会情境的迁移，并实现跨五种语言的多语言规范吸收。总之，我们的发现为LLM中持续的、以互动驱动的文化适应奠定了基础。
tldr: 本文通过沙盒环境将文化适应重新定义为一种通过重复社会互动持续吸收规范的动态过程，证明记忆机制使LLM能够在重复互动中进行纵向学习、迁移至不同社会情境，并实现跨五种语言的多语言规范吸收。
en_tdlr: This work reframes cultural adaptation as a continuous process of norm assimilation through repeated social interactions in a sandbox environment, demonstrating that memory mechanisms enable LLMs to learn longitudinally across interactions, transfer to different social settings, and assimilate norms in five languages.
